people.descriptor: Crown Prince and Imperial Family Member

label.en: director of Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs

sourceDate.text: 明宗以莊宗后夏氏妻倍

units.zh: ○義宗倍
units.en: Yizong Bei
units.literal: ○ Yizong Bei

units.zh: 〈（子平王隆先晉王道隱）〉
units.en: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)
units.literal: (Sons: Prince of Ping Longxian and Prince of Jin Daoyin)

units.zh: 章肅皇帝李胡
units.en: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu
units.literal: Emperor Zhangsu Li Hu

units.zh: 〈（子宋王喜隱）〉
units.en: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)
units.literal: (Son: Prince of Song Xiyin)

units.zh: 順宗濬晉王敖盧斡
units.en: Shunzong Jun and Prince of Jin Aolugan
units.literal: Shunzong Jun; Prince of Jin Aolugan

units.zh: 義宗，名倍，小字圖欲，太祖長子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。
units.en: Yizong, whose personal name was Bei and childhood name Tuyu, was Taizu's eldest son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
units.literal: Yizong, personal name Bei, childhood name Tuyu, eldest son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

units.zh: 幼聰敏好學，外寬內摯。
units.en: As a boy he was quick-witted and studious, mild in manner yet ardent at heart.
units.literal: In youth clever and eager to learn; outwardly lenient, inwardly earnest.

units.zh: 神冊元年春，立為皇太子。
units.en: In the spring of Shence year 1 (916) he was made crown prince.
units.literal: In spring of the first year of Shence, he was installed as crown prince.

units.zh: 時太祖問侍臣曰：「受命之君，當事天敬神。
units.en: Once Taizu asked his ministers, "A ruler who has received Heaven's mandate ought to honor Heaven and the spirits.
units.literal: At that time Taizu asked his attending ministers, saying: "A ruler who has received the Mandate should serve Heaven and revere the spirits.

units.zh: 有大功德者，朕欲祀之，何先？」
units.en: Among the figures of greatest merit, whom should I worship first?"
units.literal: Among those of great merit and virtue, whom does Your Majesty wish to sacrifice to first?"

units.zh: 皆以佛對。
units.en: They all named the Buddha.
units.literal: All answered with the Buddha.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「佛非中國教。」
units.en: Taizu said, "Buddhism is not a teaching native to China."
units.literal: Taizu said: "Buddhism is not the teaching of the Central States."

units.zh: 倍曰：「孔子大聖，萬世所尊，宜先。」
units.en: Bei replied, "Confucius is the supreme sage, revered through the ages—he should come first."
units.literal: Bei said: "Confucius the great sage, honored for ten thousand generations, should come first."

units.zh: 太祖大悅，即建孔子廟，詔皇太子春秋釋奠。
units.en: Taizu was delighted, had a Confucian temple built at once, and ordered the crown prince to conduct the spring and autumn rites of sacrifice.
units.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased, immediately built a temple to Confucius, and decreed that the crown prince perform the spring and autumn sacrificial offerings.

units.zh: 嘗從征烏古、党項，為先鋒都統，及經略燕地。
units.en: He once campaigned against the Wugu and Tangut as vanguard commander-in-chief and directed operations in the Yan region.
units.literal: He once followed campaigns against the Wugu and Tangut, served as vanguard commander-in-chief, and directed operations in the Yan region.

units.zh: 太祖西征，留倍守京師，因陳取渤海計。
units.en: When Taizu marched west, he left Bei to guard the capital and urged a plan to conquer Bohai.
units.literal: When Taizu campaigned west, he left Bei to guard the capital and presented a plan for taking Bohai.

units.zh: 天顯元年，從征渤海。
units.en: In Tianxian year 1 he joined the expedition against Bohai.
units.literal: In the first year of Tianxian he followed the campaign against Bohai.

units.zh: 拔扶餘城，上欲括戶口，倍諫曰：「今始得地而料民，民必不安。
units.en: After Fuyu city fell the emperor wished to register households; Bei remonstrated, "Having just taken the land, a census will unsettle the people.
units.literal: Fuyu city was taken; the sovereign wished to register households, and Bei remonstrated, saying, "Having just gained the land and now counting the people, the people are sure to be unsettled.

units.zh: 若乘破竹之勢，徑造忽汗城，克之必矣。」
units.en: If we press the advantage like splitting bamboo and march straight on Hohan city, we are sure to take it."
units.literal: If we ride the momentum of splitting bamboo and strike straight for Hohan city, we are certain to take it."

units.zh: 太祖從之。
units.en: Taizu accepted his advice.
units.literal: Taizu followed his counsel.

units.zh: 倍與大元帥德光為前鋒，夜圍忽汗城，大諲譔窮蹙，請降。
units.en: Bei and Great Marshal Deguang led the vanguard and besieged Hohan city by night; Dayinzan, cornered, offered surrender.
units.literal: Bei and the Great Marshal Deguang served as vanguard; they besieged Hohan city by night, and Dayinzan, hard pressed, begged to surrender.

units.zh: 尋復叛，太祖破之。
units.en: He soon rebelled again, and Taizu put him down.
units.literal: Soon he rebelled again, and Taizu defeated him.

units.zh: 改其國曰東丹，名其城曰天福，以倍為人皇王主之。
units.en: The state was renamed Eastern Dan, the city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was installed as Human Emperor King to rule it.
units.literal: Its state was renamed Eastern Dan, its city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was made Human Emperor King to rule it.

units.zh: 仍賜天子冠服，建元甘露，稱制，置左右大次四相及百官，一用漢法。
units.en: He was also granted imperial cap and robes, adopted the era name Ganlu, ruled in his own right, and set up left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the full bureaucracy—all on the Han model.
units.literal: He was further granted the cap and robes of the Son of Heaven, adopted the era name Ganlu, exercised regency, and established left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the hundred offices—all following Han institutions.

units.zh: 歲貢布十五萬端，馬千匹。
units.en: Each year he paid tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.
units.literal: Each year he rendered tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.

units.zh: 上諭曰：「此地瀕海，非可久居，留汝撫治，以見朕愛民之心。」
units.en: The emperor told him, "This land lies on the sea and cannot be held long; I leave you to govern it and show my care for the people."
units.literal: The sovereign instructed him, saying, "This land borders the sea and cannot be long occupied; I leave you to govern and soothe it, that my love for the people may be seen."

units.zh: 駕將還，倍作歌以獻。
units.en: As the emperor prepared to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.
units.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.

units.zh: 陛辭，太祖曰：「得汝治東土，吾復何憂。」
units.en: As he took leave at court, Taizu said, "With you governing the east, what have I left to fear?"
units.literal: Taking leave at the steps, Taizu said, "With you governing the eastern lands, what further worry have I?"

units.zh: 倍號泣而出。
units.en: Bei wept aloud as he departed.
units.literal: Bei wailed and wept as he went out.

units.zh: 遂如儀坤州。
units.en: He then went on to Yikun Prefecture as ordered.
units.literal: He then proceeded to Yikun Prefecture as prescribed.

units.zh: 未幾，諸部多叛，大元帥討平之。
units.en: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal put them down.
units.literal: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal suppressed and pacified them.

units.zh: 太祖訃至，倍即日奔赴山陵。
units.en: When word of Taizu's death arrived, Bei set out the same day for the imperial tomb.
units.literal: When Taizu's death notice arrived, Bei set out that same day to hurry to the imperial tomb.

units.zh: 倍知皇太后意欲立德光，乃謂公卿曰：「大元帥功德及人神，中外攸屬，宜主社稷。」
units.en: Knowing the Empress Dowager meant to elevate Deguang, Bei told the chief ministers, "The Great Marshal's achievements touch both men and spirits; court and country alike look to him—he ought to rule the realm."
units.literal: Bei knew the Empress Dowager wished to install Deguang, and therefore said to the dukes and ministers: "The Great Marshal's merit reaches men and spirits; within and without all look to him—he should hold the altars of state."

units.zh: 乃與群臣請於太后而讓位焉。
units.en: He and the officials petitioned the Empress Dowager, and he yielded the throne.
units.literal: He then joined the officials in petitioning the Empress Dowager and yielded the throne.

units.zh: 於是大元帥即皇帝位，是為太宗。
units.en: The Great Marshal then took the throne as Emperor Taizong.
units.literal: Thereupon the Great Marshal assumed the imperial position—this was Taizong.

units.zh: 太宗既立，見疑，以東平為南京，徙倍居之，盡遷其民。
units.en: After Taizong's accession Bei fell under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was relocated there, and the entire population was moved away.
units.literal: Once Taizong was established, Bei came under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was moved to dwell there, and all its people were relocated.

units.zh: 又置衛士陰伺動靜。
units.en: Guards were also set to spy on his movements in secret.
units.literal: Guards were also posted to watch his movements in secret.

units.zh: 倍既歸國，命王繼遠撰《建南京碑》，起書樓於西宮，作《樂田園詩》。
units.en: Once back in his domain, Bei had Wang Jiyuan draft the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," built a book tower in the Western Palace, and composed "Joy in the Garden."
units.literal: After Bei returned to his domain, he ordered Wang Jiyuan to compose the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," raised a book tower in the Western Palace, and wrote the poem "Joy in the Garden."

units.zh: 唐明宗聞之，遣人跨海持書密召倍。
units.en: When Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of it, he sent envoys across the sea with a secret letter inviting Bei.
units.literal: Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of this and sent men across the sea with a letter to summon Bei in secret.

units.zh: 倍因畋海上。
units.en: Bei happened to be hunting at sea.
units.literal: Bei happened to be hunting on the sea.

units.zh: 使再至，倍謂左右曰：「我以天下讓主上，今反見疑；
units.en: When the envoys came again, Bei told his attendants, "I gave the empire to our sovereign, yet now I am distrusted;
units.literal: When the envoys came a second time, Bei said to those beside him: "I yielded the realm to our lord; now I am met with suspicion instead;

units.zh: 不如適他國，以成吳太伯之名。」
units.en: better to go abroad and earn a name like Wu Taibo's."
units.literal: better to go to another state and fulfill the name of Wu Taibo."

units.zh: 立木海上，刻詩曰：「小山壓大山，大山全無力。
units.en: He erected a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill weighs on the great hill—the great hill has no strength at all.
units.literal: He set up a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill presses the great hill; the great hill is wholly without strength.

units.zh: 羞見故鄉人，從此投外國。」
units.en: Too ashamed to face the folk of home—from this I go to a foreign land."
units.literal: Ashamed to face the people of my homeland, from this I cast myself to a foreign land."

units.zh: 攜高美人，載書浮海而去。
units.en: Taking Lady Gao with him, he loaded his books and sailed away across the sea.
units.literal: Taking Lady Gao the fair, he loaded his books and went off across the sea.

units.zh: 唐以天子儀衛迎倍，倍坐船殿，眾官陪列上壽。
units.en: Tang received Bei with imperial ceremonial guard; he sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering congratulations.
units.literal: Tang received Bei with the ceremonial guard of the Son of Heaven; Bei sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering longevity wishes.

units.zh: 至汴，見明宗。
units.en: On reaching Bian he was received by Emperor Mingzong.
units.literal: Reaching Bian, he met Mingzong.

units.zh: 明宗以莊宗后夏氏妻之，賜姓東丹，名之曰慕華。
units.en: Mingzong gave him Zhuangzong's consort, Lady Xia, in marriage and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.
units.literal: Mingzong gave him in marriage Empress Xia of Zhuangzong and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.

units.zh: 改瑞州為懷化軍，拜懷化軍節度使、瑞慎等州觀察使。
units.en: Ruizhou was made Huaihua Army, and he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.
units.literal: Ruizhou was changed to Huaihua Army; he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 復賜姓李，名贊華。
units.en: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.
units.literal: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.

units.zh: 移鎮滑州，遙領虔州節度使。
units.en: He was transferred to Huazhou and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.
units.literal: He was transferred to garrison Huazhou and held concurrently the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.

units.zh: 倍雖在異國，常思其親，問安之使不絕。
units.en: Though abroad, Bei never ceased thinking of his family, and messengers sending greetings home never stopped.
units.literal: Though Bei was in a foreign land, he constantly thought of his kin, and envoys sending inquiries after their welfare never ceased.

units.zh: 後明宗養子從珂弒其君自立，倍密報太宗曰：「從珂弒君，盍討之。」
units.en: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized power; Bei secretly informed Taizong, "Congke has murdered his lord—we ought to punish him."
units.literal: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized the throne; Bei secretly reported to Taizong, saying, "Congke murdered his lord—why not punish him?"

units.zh: 及太宗立石敬瑭為晉主，加兵於洛。
units.en: When Taizong set up Shi Jingtang as Jin emperor and sent additional troops against Luoyang.
units.literal: When Taizong installed Shi Jingtang as Jin sovereign and added troops at Luoyang.

units.zh: 從珂欲自焚，召倍與俱，倍不從，遣壯士李彥紳害之，時年三十八。
units.en: Congke meant to burn himself and summoned Bei to die with him; Bei refused, and Congke sent the strongman Li Yanzhen to kill him. Bei was thirty-eight.
units.literal: Congke wished to burn himself, summoned Bei to join him, and Bei refused; he sent the strong man Li Yanzhen to kill him—he was thirty-eight years old.

units.zh: 有一僧為收瘞之。
units.en: A monk gathered and buried his remains.
units.literal: A monk gathered and buried his remains.

units.zh: 敬瑭入洛，喪服臨哭，以王禮權厝。
units.en: When Jingtang entered Luoyang he came in mourning to weep at the coffin and provisionally interred Bei with royal rites.
units.literal: Jingtang entered Luoyang, came in mourning garb to weep before the coffin, and provisionally interred him with the rites due a king.

units.zh: 後太宗改葬於醫巫閭山，謚曰文武元皇王。
units.en: Later Taizong had him reburied on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously styled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.
units.literal: Later Taizong reburied him on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously titled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.

units.zh: 世宗即位，謚讓國皇帝，陵曰顯陵。
units.en: When Shizong succeeded, Bei was posthumously styled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was named Xianling.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was called Xianling.

units.zh: 統和中，更謚文獻。
units.en: In the Tonghe era his posthumous title was changed to Wenxian.
units.literal: During Tonghe his title was changed to Wenxian.

units.zh: 重熙二十年，增謚文獻欽義皇帝，廟號義宗，及謚二后曰端順，曰柔貞。
units.en: In Chongxi year 20 his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and his two consorts were posthumously styled Duanshun and Rouzhen.
units.literal: In the twentieth year of Chongxi his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and the two empresses were posthumously titled Duanshun and Rouzhen.

units.zh: 倍初市書至萬卷，藏於醫巫閭絕頂之望海堂。
units.en: Bei had once bought books until his collection reached ten thousand scrolls, which he kept in the Wanghai Hall on the summit of Mount Yiwulü.
units.literal: Bei at first bought books until they reached ten thousand scrolls, storing them in the Wanghai Hall atop the summit of Mount Yiwulü.

units.zh: 通陰陽，知音律，精醫藥、砭焫之術。
units.en: He understood yin and yang, knew music and pitch, and was skilled in medicine, acupuncture, and moxibustion.
units.literal: He mastered yin and yang, understood music and pitch, and was expert in medicine and the arts of acupuncture and moxibustion.

units.zh: 工遼、漢文章，嘗譯《陰符經》。
units.en: He wrote well in both Khitan and Chinese and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."
units.literal: He was accomplished in Khitan and Han writing and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."

units.zh: 善畫本國人物，如《射騎》、《獵雪騎》、《千鹿圖》，皆入宋秘府。
units.en: He excelled at painting Khitan subjects; works such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer" all entered the Song imperial collection.
units.literal: He was skilled at painting figures of his own country, such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer"—all entered the Song imperial treasury.

units.zh: 然性刻急好殺，婢妾微過，常加刲灼。
units.en: Yet he was harsh and quick-tempered and prone to cruelty; for the slightest slip by maids or concubines he often branded or cauterized them.
units.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and impatient and he loved killing; for slight faults in maidservants and concubines he often applied branding and cautery.

units.zh: 夏氏懼而求削髮為尼。
units.en: Lady Xia, terrified, begged to shave her head and take vows as a nun.
units.literal: Lady Xia, in fear, begged to shave her head and become a nun.

units.zh: 五子：長世宗，次婁國、稍、隆先、道隱，各有傳。
units.en: He had five sons: the eldest was Shizong, followed by Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each treated in his own biography.
units.literal: Five sons: the eldest Shizong, next Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each has a separate biography.

units.zh: 平王隆先，字團隱，母大氏。
units.en: Longxian, Prince of Ping, whose style was Tuanyin, was born to the Da clan.
units.literal: Prince of Ping Longxian, style Tuanyin, mother the Da clan.

units.zh: 景宗即位，始封平王。
units.en: When Jingzong succeeded he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.
units.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.

units.zh: 未幾，兼政事令，留守東京。
units.en: Soon afterward he was made chief of governmental affairs while also serving as regent of the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Before long he concurrently served as chief of governmental affairs and remained to guard the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 薄賦稅，省刑獄，恤鰥寡，數薦賢能之士。
units.en: He eased taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for the widowed and orphaned, and repeatedly recommended able men.
units.literal: He lightened taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for widowers and widows, and repeatedly recommended worthy and capable men.

units.zh: 後與統軍耶律室魯同討高麗有功，還薨，葬醫巫閭山之道隱谷。
units.en: Later he joined army commander Yelu Shilu in a successful campaign against Goryeo; on his return he died and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.
units.literal: Later he campaigned against Goryeo together with army commander Yelu Shilu with merit; returning, he died, and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.

units.zh: 平王為人聰明，博學能詩，有《閬苑集》行於世。
units.en: The Prince of Ping was clever, broadly learned, and skilled in poetry; his Collection of the Lang Garden circulated widely.
units.literal: Prince of Ping was clever by nature, broadly learned and skilled in poetry; his "Collection of the Lang Garden" circulated in the world.

units.zh: 保寧之季，其子陳哥與渤海官屬謀殺其父，舉兵作亂，上命轘裂於市。
units.en: Late in the Baoning era his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to murder him and rose in rebellion; the emperor ordered Chenge executed by dismemberment in the market.
units.literal: Late in Baoning his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to kill his father, raised troops in rebellion, and the sovereign ordered him torn apart by carriages in the market.

units.zh: 晉王道隱，字留隱，母高氏。
units.en: Daoyin, Prince of Jin, whose style was Liuyin, was born to the Gao clan.
units.literal: Prince of Jin Daoyin, style Liuyin, mother the Gao clan.

units.zh: 道隱生於唐，人皇王遭李從珂之害，時年尚幼，洛陽僧匿而養之，因名道隱。
units.en: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King was killed by Li Congke he was still a child, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.
units.literal: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King met harm at the hands of Li Congke he was still young, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.

units.zh: 太宗滅唐，還京，詔賜外羅山地居焉。
units.en: After Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him residence on Mount Wailuo.
units.literal: When Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him land on Mount Wailuo to dwell.

units.zh: 性沈靜，有文武才，時人稱之。
units.en: Calm and reserved by nature, he had both civil and military talent, and contemporaries praised him.
units.literal: His nature was calm and reserved; he had civil and military talent, and men of the time praised him.

units.zh: 景宗即位，封蜀王，為上京留守。
units.en: When Jingzong succeeded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and appointed regent of the Upper Capital.
units.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and made regent of the Upper Capital.

units.zh: 乾亨元年，遷守南京，號令嚴肅，民獲安業。
units.en: In Qianheng year 1 he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his rule was strict and orderly, and the people lived in peace.
units.literal: In the first year of Qianheng he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his orders were stern and disciplined, and the people found security in their livelihoods.

units.zh: 居數年，徙封荊王。
units.en: After several years his title was changed to Prince of Jing.
units.literal: After several years he was moved to the enfeoffment of Prince of Jing.

units.zh: 統和初，病薨，追封晉王。
units.en: Early in the Tonghe era he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
units.literal: Early in Tonghe he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 論曰：自古新造之國，一傳而太子讓，豈易得哉？
units.en: Commentary: In newly founded states since antiquity, how rare it is for a crown prince to yield the throne in the very first succession!
units.literal: The commentary says: Since antiquity in newly founded states, for the crown prince to yield in a single transmission—how easily is that attained?

units.zh: 遼之義宗，可謂盛矣！
units.en: Liao's Yizong stands among the finest examples!
units.literal: Liao's Yizong may be called magnificent!

units.zh: 然讓而見疑，豈不兆於建元稱制之際乎？
units.en: Yet once he had yielded he was distrusted—was that not already foreshadowed when he adopted an era name and ruled in his own right?
units.literal: Yet after yielding he met with suspicion—was this not foreshadowed at the time he established an era name and exercised regency?

units.zh: 斯則一時君臣昧於禮制之過也。
units.en: That was a lapse of ruler and ministers alike, who failed to grasp proper ritual and institutions.
units.literal: This was a fault of ruler and ministers of that age, blind to ritual and institutions.

units.zh: 束書浮海，寄跡他國，思親不忘，問安不絕，其心甚有足諒者焉。
units.en: He packed his books and crossed the sea to live abroad, yet never forgot his family and kept sending greetings home—there is much in his heart that deserves understanding.
units.literal: Bundling his books and crossing the sea, lodging his footsteps in another state, he did not forget his kin and never ceased sending inquiries after their welfare—his heart has much that may be forgiven.

units.zh: 觀其始慕泰伯之賢而為遠適之謀，終疾陳恒之惡而有請討之舉，誌趣之卓，蓋已見於早歲先祀孔子之言歟。
units.en: See how early on he admired Taibo's virtue and planned exile abroad, and in the end loathed Chen Heng's crime and urged his ruler to punish it—his high purpose was already plain in youth, when he argued to honor Confucius first.
units.literal: Observe how at first he admired Taibo's virtue and made plans for distant departure, and at the end detested Chen Heng's wickedness and urged a punitive campaign—his lofty aims were already seen in his early years in the words that put Confucius first in sacrifice.

units.zh: 善不令終，天道難詰，得非性卞嗜殺之所致也？
units.en: Virtue did not win him a gentle end; Heaven's ways are hard to fathom—was it not his harsh, bloodthirsty temper that brought it about?
units.literal: Goodness did not bring him a peaceful end; Heaven's way is hard to question—was it not caused by a harsh nature and love of killing?

units.zh: 雖然，終遼之代，賢聖繼統，皆其子孫。
units.en: Even so, through the entire Liao dynasty the worthy and sage who held the throne were all his descendants.
units.literal: Even so, through the whole Liao age, worthy and sage rulers succeeded one another—all were his descendants.

units.zh: 至德之報，昭然在茲矣。
units.en: The reward of supreme virtue shines plainly in this.
units.literal: The reward of supreme virtue is manifest here.

units.zh: 章肅皇帝，小字李胡，一名洪古，字奚隱，太祖第三子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。
units.en: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, also called Honggu, style Xiyin, was Taizu's third son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
units.literal: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, another name Honggu, style Xiyin, third son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

units.zh: 少勇悍多力，而性殘酷，小怒輒黥人面，或投水火中。
units.en: As a youth he was fierce and powerful, but cruel by nature; the least provocation could bring facial tattooing or being thrown into water or fire.
units.literal: In youth brave, fierce, and strong, yet cruel by nature; at a slight anger he would tattoo faces or cast people into water or fire.

units.zh: 太祖嘗觀諸子寢，李胡縮項臥內，曰：「是必在諸子下。」
units.en: Taizu once watched his sons sleep. Li Hu lay curled up with his neck drawn in, and Taizu said, "This one will surely rank below his brothers."
units.literal: Taizu once watched his sons sleep; Li Hu lay inside with neck drawn in, and said: "This one is sure to rank below the other sons."

units.zh: 又嘗大寒，命三子采薪。
units.en: On another bitterly cold day he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.
units.literal: On another occasion in severe cold he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.

units.zh: 太宗不擇而取，最先至；
units.en: Taizong gathered without picking and came back first;
units.literal: Taizong took without choosing and arrived first;

units.zh: 人皇王取其乾者束而歸，後至；
units.en: the Human Emperor King chose the dry wood, bound it into a bundle, and returned later;
units.literal: the Human Emperor King took the dry pieces, bound them, and returned, arriving later;

units.zh: 李胡取少而棄多，既至，袖手而立。
units.en: Li Hu took little and threw away much; when he arrived he stood with empty hands in his sleeves.
units.literal: Li Hu took little and discarded much; when he arrived he stood with hands in sleeves.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「長巧而次成，少不及矣。」
units.en: Taizu said, "The eldest is clever, the second gets things done; the youngest falls short."
units.literal: Taizu said: "The eldest is clever, the second accomplishes; the youngest does not measure up."

units.zh: 而母篤愛李胡。
units.en: Yet his mother doted on Li Hu.
units.literal: Yet the mother dearly loved Li Hu.

units.zh: 天顯五年，遣徇地代北，攻寰州，多俘而還，遂立為皇太弟，兼天下兵馬大元帥。
units.en: In Tianxian year 5 he was sent to campaign in the Dai north, attacked Huan Prefecture, returned with many captives, and was made Imperial Younger Brother Heir while also serving as commander-in-chief of all forces.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxian he was sent to traverse the land north of Dai, attacked Huan Prefecture, took many captives and returned, and was then installed as Imperial Younger Brother Heir and concurrently Great Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

units.zh: 太宗親征，常留守京師。
units.en: Whenever Taizong led campaigns in person, Li Hu usually stayed behind as regent in the capital.
units.literal: When Taizong campaigned in person, he regularly remained to guard the capital.

units.zh: 世宗即位鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡將兵擊之。
units.en: When Shizong assumed the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager in anger sent Li Hu with an army against him.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager was angry and sent Li Hu to lead troops against him.

units.zh: 至泰德泉，為安端、留哥所敗。
units.en: At Taidé Spring he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.
units.literal: Reaching Taidé Spring, he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.

units.zh: 太后與世宗隔潢河而陣，各言舉兵意。
units.en: The Empress Dowager and Shizong drew up on opposite banks of the Huang River and each explained why he had taken up arms.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager and Shizong faced each other across the Huang River in battle array, each stating the reason for raising troops.

units.zh: 耶律屋質入諫太后曰：「主上已立，宜許之。」
units.en: Yelü Wuzhi went in and urged the Empress Dowager, "The emperor is already enthroned—you ought to accept him."
units.literal: Yelü Wuzhi entered and remonstrated with the Empress Dowager, saying: "The sovereign is already established—you should acknowledge him."

units.zh: 時李胡在側，作色曰：「我在，兀欲安得立？」
units.en: Li Hu stood at her side, flushed with anger, and said, "As long as I live, how can Wuyue take the throne?"
units.literal: At that time Li Hu was at her side; he changed color and said: "While I am here, how can Wuyue be established?"

units.zh: 屋質曰：「奈公酷暴失人心何！」
units.en: Wuzhi replied, "What can be done when you are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts?"
units.literal: Wuzhi said: "What of it that you, sir, are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts!"

units.zh: 太后顧李胡曰：「昔我與太祖愛汝異於諸子，諺云：『偏憐之子不保業，難得之婦不主家。』
units.en: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said, "Taizu and I once loved you more than your brothers. As the proverb runs, 'The child too fondly indulged cannot keep the estate; the wife too hard won cannot keep the house.'
units.literal: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said: "In the past I and Taizu loved you differently from the other sons. A proverb says: 'A child over-favored cannot keep the estate; a wife hard to win does not manage the household.'

units.zh: 我非不欲立汝，汝自不能矣。」
units.en: It is not that I would not make you emperor—you simply could not hold it."
units.literal: It is not that I did not wish to install you—you yourself could not do it."

units.zh: 及會議，世宗使解劍而言。
units.en: At the council Shizong had his sword taken before he addressed them.
units.literal: When they met in council, Shizong had his sword removed before he spoke.

units.zh: 和約既定，趨上京。
units.en: Once peace was agreed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.
units.literal: Once the peace pact was fixed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.

units.zh: 會有告李胡與太后謀廢立者，徙李胡祖州，禁其出入。
units.en: When word came that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager were plotting to depose the emperor, Li Hu was exiled to Zuzhou and forbidden to leave.
units.literal: Soon someone reported that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager plotted deposition and installation; Li Hu was moved to Zuzhou and his coming and going forbidden.

units.zh: 穆宗時，其子喜隱謀反，辭逮李胡，囚之，死獄中，年五十，葬玉峰山西谷。
units.en: Under Muzong his son Xiyin rebelled; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at fifty, and was buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.
units.literal: In Muzong's time his son Xiyin plotted rebellion; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at age fifty, buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.

units.zh: 統和中，追謚欽順皇帝。
units.en: In the Tonghe era he was posthumously styled Emperor Qinshun.
units.literal: During Tonghe he was posthumously titled Emperor Qinshun.

units.zh: 重熙二十一年，更謚章肅，后曰和敬。
units.en: In Chongxi year 21 his title was changed to Zhangsu; his consort was styled Hejing.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi the title was changed to Zhangsu; the consort was called Hejing.

units.zh: 二子：宋王喜隱、衛王宛。
units.en: He had two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.
units.literal: Two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.

units.zh: 喜隱，字完德，雄偉善騎射，封趙王。
units.en: Xiyin, whose style was Wande, was imposing and skilled in mounted archery and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
units.literal: Xiyin, style Wande, imposing and skilled in mounted archery, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

units.zh: 應歷中，謀反，事覺，上臨問有狀，以親釋之。
units.en: During the Yingli era he plotted rebellion; when the plot was exposed the emperor questioned him in person, found the charge proved, yet released him as a kinsman.
units.literal: During Yingli he plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered the sovereign questioned him in person and found the facts established, yet released him because of kinship.

units.zh: 未幾，復反，下獄。
units.en: Before long he rebelled again and was thrown into prison.
units.literal: Before long he rebelled again and was cast into prison.

units.zh: 景宗即位，聞有赦，自去其械而朝。
units.en: When Jingzong succeeded, hearing that an amnesty had been declared, he removed his own shackles and came to court.
units.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, hearing there was an amnesty, he removed his own fetters and came to court.

units.zh: 上怒曰：「汝罪人，何得擅離禁所！」
units.en: The emperor angrily said, "You are a convicted man—how dare you leave confinement on your own!"
units.literal: The sovereign in anger said, "You are a criminal—how dare you leave your place of confinement on your own!"

units.zh: 詔誅守者，復置於獄。
units.en: An edict ordered the guards put to death, and he was returned to prison.
units.literal: An edict ordered the guards executed, and he was again placed in prison.

units.zh: 及改元保寧，乃宥之，妻以皇后之姊，復爵，王宋。
units.en: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, married to the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.
units.literal: When the era was changed to Baoning he was pardoned, given in marriage the empress's elder sister, restored to rank, and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.

units.zh: 喜隱輕僄無恒，小得志即驕。
units.en: Xiyin was frivolous and unreliable; the least success made him arrogant.
units.literal: Xiyin was frivolous and inconstant; with the slightest success he grew arrogant.

units.zh: 上嘗召，不時至，怒而鞭之，由是憤怨謀亂。
units.en: Once when the emperor summoned him he failed to come promptly; the emperor in anger had him flogged, and from then on he nursed resentment and plotted rebellion.
units.literal: The sovereign once summoned him and he did not come promptly; in anger the sovereign flogged him, and from this he nursed resentment and plotted disorder.

units.zh: 貶而復召，適見上與劉繼元書，辭意卑遜，諫曰：「本朝於漢為祖，書旨如此，恐虧國體。」
units.en: Though demoted he was summoned again; seeing the emperor's letter to Liu Jiyuan, whose tone was abject, he remonstrated, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—with wording like this, the dignity of the state will suffer."
units.literal: Demoted yet summoned again, he happened to see the sovereign's letter to Liu Jiyuan, its wording humble and submissive, and remonstrated, saying, "Our dynasty is ancestor to Han—if the letter's intent is thus, I fear the dignity of the state will be impaired."

units.zh: 帝尋改之。
units.en: The emperor soon revised the letter.
units.literal: The emperor soon revised it.

units.zh: 授西南面招討使，命之河東索吐蕃戶，稍見進用。
units.en: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and sent east of the river to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually won greater favor.
units.literal: He was appointed southwestern frontier pacification commissioner and ordered to the east of the Yellow River to seek out Tibetan households; he gradually came into favor.

units.zh: 復誘群小謀叛，上命械其手足，築圜土，囚祖州。
units.en: He again incited petty followers to rebel; the emperor ordered his limbs shackled, a round-walled cell built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.
units.literal: He again enticed petty men to plot rebellion; the sovereign ordered his hands and feet shackled, a round-walled enclosure built, and him imprisoned at Zuzhou.

units.zh: 宋降卒二百餘人欲劫立喜隱，以城堅不得入，立其子留禮壽，上京留守除室擒之。
units.en: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers tried to seize the city and install Xiyin; failing to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou instead; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.
units.literal: More than two hundred surrendered Song soldiers wished to seize and install Xiyin; unable to enter because the walls were strong, they installed his son Liulishou; Upper Capital regent Chushi captured him.

units.zh: 留禮壽伏誅，賜喜隱死。
units.en: Liulishou was put to death, and Xiyin was sentenced to death.
units.literal: Liulishou was executed, and Xiyin was granted death.

units.zh: 論曰：李胡殘酷驕盈，太祖知其不才而不能教，太后不知其惡而溺愛之。
units.en: Commentary: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant. Taizu knew he lacked talent but could not teach him; the Empress Dowager did not see his wickedness and spoiled him.
units.literal: The commentary says: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant; Taizu knew he lacked talent yet could not instruct him, and the Empress Dowager did not know his wickedness and doted on him.

units.zh: 初以屋質之言定立世宗，而復謀廢立。
units.en: At first Wuzhi's counsel secured Shizong's enthronement, yet mother and son plotted deposition again.
units.literal: At first through Wuzhi's words Shizong's enthronement was settled, yet they again plotted deposition and installation.

units.zh: 子孫繼以逆誅，並及其身，可哀也已。
units.en: Descendants were executed one after another for treason, and ruin reached him as well—a lamentable end.
units.literal: Descendants in succession met execution for treason, reaching even to his person—pitiable indeed.

units.zh: 夫自太祖之世，剌葛、安端首倡禍亂，太祖既不之誅，又復用之，固為有君人之量，然惟太祖之才足以駕馭，庶乎其可也。
units.en: From Taizu's reign Cige and Anduan were the first to stir rebellion; Taizu neither executed them outright nor cast them off permanently, which showed true magnanimity as a ruler—yet only Taizu's ability could keep them in hand, and even that was barely enough.
units.literal: From Taizu's age, Cige and Anduan first raised calamity and disorder; Taizu neither punished them to the full, yet employed them again—this truly showed the measure of a ruler of men, yet only Taizu's talent could rein them in; perhaps that could suffice.

units.zh: 李胡而下，宗王反側，無代無之，遼之內難，與國始終。
units.en: From Li Hu onward, imperial princes were forever restless; no reign was free of it—Liao's internal strife dogged the dynasty from start to finish.
units.literal: From Li Hu downward, imperial princes were restless; no reign lacked this—Liao's internal troubles ran with the state from beginning to end.

units.zh: 厥後嗣君，雖嚴法以繩之，卒不可止。
units.en: Later emperors bound them with harsh law, yet still could not stop it.
units.literal: Later successor rulers, though they bound them with stern law, ultimately could not stop it.

units.zh: 烏乎，創業垂統之主，所以貽厥孫謀者，可不審歟！
units.en: Alas! Founders who establish a dynasty and pass it on—what they leave their heirs demands the utmost care!
units.literal: Alas! A founding ruler who hands down the succession—what he bequeaths to his descendants' plans: can it go unexamined!

units.zh: 順宗，名濬，小字耶魯斡，道宗長子，母宣懿皇后蕭氏。
units.en: Shunzong, whose personal name was Jun and childhood name Yeluwo, was Daozong's eldest son; his mother was Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.
units.literal: Shunzong, personal name Jun, childhood name Yeluwo, eldest son of Daozong, mother Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan.

units.zh: 幼而能言，好學知書。
units.en: As a child he could speak early, loved learning, and was well read.
units.literal: As a child he could speak; he loved learning and knew books.

units.zh: 道宗嘗曰：「此子聰慧，殆天授歟！」
units.en: Daozong once said, "This boy is clever—perhaps Heaven itself bestowed it!"
units.literal: Daozong once said, "This child is clever—perhaps Heaven bestowed it!"

units.zh: 六歲，封梁王。
units.en: At six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
units.literal: At age six he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.

units.zh: 明年，從上獵，矢連發三中。
units.en: The next year he joined the emperor on a hunt and with three arrows in swift succession scored three hits.
units.literal: The next year he followed the sovereign on a hunt and with arrows in swift succession hit three times.

units.zh: 上顧左右曰：「朕祖宗以來，騎射絕人，威震天下。
units.en: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Since my ancestors, our horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and our might has shaken the realm.
units.literal: The sovereign turned to those beside him and said, "From my ancestors onward, horsemanship and archery have been unmatched and awe has shaken the realm.

units.zh: 是兒雖幼，不墜其風。」
units.en: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."
units.literal: Though this boy is young, he does not fall short of that tradition."

units.zh: 後遇十鹿，射獲其九。
units.en: Later, meeting ten deer, he brought down nine.
units.literal: Later encountering ten deer, he shot and took nine.

units.zh: 帝喜，設宴。
units.en: Delighted, the emperor held a banquet.
units.literal: The emperor was pleased and held a banquet.

units.zh: 八歲，立為皇太子。
units.en: At eight he was made crown prince.
units.literal: At age eight he was installed as crown prince.

units.zh: 大康元年，兼領北南樞密院事。
units.en: In Dakang year 1 he also took charge of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.
units.literal: In the first year of Dakang he concurrently directed the affairs of the Northern and Southern Bureaus of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 及母后被害，太子有憂色。
units.en: When the empress mother was killed, the crown prince's face showed deep worry.
units.literal: When the empress mother was murdered, the crown prince wore a troubled look.

units.zh: 耶律乙辛為北院樞密使，常不自安。
units.en: Yelü Yixin, Northern Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was constantly uneasy.
units.literal: Yelü Yixin served as Northern Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was often ill at ease.

units.zh: 會護衛蕭忽古謀害乙辛，事覺，下獄。
units.en: When guard Xiao Hugu plotted to kill Yixin, the plot was exposed and he was thrown into prison.
units.literal: It happened that guard Xiao Hugu plotted to kill Yixin; the affair was discovered and he was cast into prison.

units.zh: 副點檢蕭十三謂乙辛曰：「臣民心屬太子，公非閥閱，一日若立，吾輩措身何地！」
units.en: Deputy Inspector Xiao Shisan told Yixin, "Officials and commoners alike look to the crown prince. You are not of high birth—once he reigns, where will men like us stand?"
units.literal: Deputy Inspector Xiao Shisan said to Yixin: "Officials and people look to the crown prince; you, sir, are not of noble pedigree—if he ascends one day, where shall we place ourselves!"

units.zh: 乃與同知北院宣徽事蕭特裏特謀構陷太子，陰令右護衛太保耶律查剌誣告都宮使耶律撒剌、知院蕭速撒、護衛蕭忽古謀廢立。
units.en: He and Associate Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Palace Attendants Xiao Telite then plotted to frame the crown prince, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse Palace Director Yelü Sala, Commissioner Xiao Susa, and guard Xiao Hugu of plotting a coup.
units.literal: He then joined Associate Commissioner of the Northern Bureau of Palace Attendants Xiao Telite in plotting to frame the crown prince, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse falsely Palace Director Yelü Sala, Commissioner Xiao Susa, and guard Xiao Hugu of plotting deposition and installation.

units.zh: 詔案無跡，不治。
units.en: An imperial inquiry found no evidence, and the case was dropped.
units.literal: An imperial order investigated and found no trace; the case was not pursued.

units.zh: 乙辛復令牌印郎君蕭訛都斡等言：「查剌前告非妄，臣實與謀，欲殺耶律乙辛等，然後立太子。
units.en: Yixin then had Seal and Insignia Attendant Xiao Eduogan and others declare, "Chala's first report was true—I was in the plot to kill Yelü Yixin and his faction, then put the crown prince on the throne.
units.literal: Yixin again ordered Seal and Insignia Attendant Xiao Eduogan and others to say: "Chala's earlier accusation was not false; I truly joined the plot, intending to kill Yelü Yixin and the rest, and then install the crown prince.

units.zh: 臣若不言，恐事發連坐。」
units.en: If I do not confess now, I fear I will be punished when the plot is uncovered."
units.literal: If your servant does not speak, I fear that when the affair breaks out I will be implicated by association."

units.zh: 帝信之，幽太子於別室，以耶律燕哥鞫案。
units.en: The emperor believed them, confined the crown prince in a separate room, and put Yelü Yange in charge of the investigation.
units.literal: The emperor believed it, confined the crown prince in a separate chamber, and had Yelü Yange conduct the inquest.

units.zh: 太子具陳枉狀曰：「吾為儲副，尚何所求。
units.en: The crown prince laid out the injustice of the charge: "I am heir apparent—what more could I want?
units.literal: The crown prince fully stated the injustice of the case, saying: "I am heir apparent—what more could I seek?

units.zh: 公當為我辨之。」
units.en: You must speak for me."
units.literal: You, sir, ought to clear me."

units.zh: 燕哥乃乙辛之黨，易其言為款伏。
units.en: Yange was Yixin's man and twisted his words into a confession.
units.literal: Yange was of Yixin's faction and altered his words into a confession.

units.zh: 上大怒，廢太子為庶人。
units.en: The emperor flew into a rage and deposed the crown prince to commoner status.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and deposed the crown prince to commoner status.

units.zh: 將出，曰：「我何罪至是！」
units.en: As he was led out he cried, "What crime have I committed to deserve this!"
units.literal: As he was about to go out, he said: "What crime of mine reaches this!"

units.zh: 十三叱登車，遣衛士闔其扉。
units.en: Shisan shouted at him to get in the carriage and had guards slam the doors shut.
units.literal: Shisan shouted at him to mount the carriage and sent guards to shut the doors.

units.zh: 徙於上京，囚圜堵中。
units.en: He was exiled to the Upper Capital and held in a round-walled cell.
units.literal: He was moved to the Upper Capital and imprisoned within a round enclosure.

units.zh: 乙辛尋遣達魯古、撒八往害之，太子年方二十，上京留守蕭撻得紿以疾薨聞。
units.en: Yixin soon sent Dalugu and Saba to kill him. The crown prince was only twenty; Upper Capital regent Xiao Tade was tricked with a report that he had died of illness.
units.literal: Yixin soon sent Dalugu and Saba to go and harm him; the crown prince was only twenty years old; the Upper Capital regent Xiao Tade was deceived with a report that he had died of illness.

units.zh: 上哀之，命有司葬龍門山。
units.en: The emperor grieved and ordered an official burial at Longmen Mountain.
units.literal: The emperor mourned him and ordered the authorities to bury him at Longmen Mountain.

units.zh: 欲召其妃，乙辛陰遣人殺之。
units.en: When he wished to summon the crown prince's consort, Yixin secretly had her murdered.
units.literal: He wished to summon the crown prince's consort; Yixin secretly sent men to kill her.

units.zh: 帝後知其冤，悔恨無及，謚曰昭懷太子，以天子禮改葬玉峰山。
units.en: When the emperor later learned of the injustice, remorse came too late. He posthumously styled him Crown Prince Zhaohuai and reburied him on Mount Yufeng with imperial rites.
units.literal: Later the emperor learned of his injustice; regret came too late. He was posthumously titled Crown Prince Zhaohuai and reburied at Mount Yufeng with rites due an emperor.

units.zh: 乾統初，追尊大孝順聖皇帝，廟號順宗，妃蕭氏貞順皇后。
units.en: At the start of the Qian Tong era he was posthumously elevated to Emperor the Great Filial and Shun the Sage, with temple name Shunzong; his consort of the Xiao clan was styled Empress Zhenshun.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qian Tong he was posthumously honored as Emperor the Great Filial and Shun the Sage; temple name Shunzong; consort of the Xiao clan, Empress Zhenshun.

units.zh: 一子，延禧，即天祚皇帝。
units.en: He had one son, Yanxi, who became Emperor Tianzuo.
units.literal: One son, Yanxi—that is, Emperor Tianzuo.

units.zh: 論曰：道宗知太子之賢，而不能辨乙辛之詐，竟絕父子之親，為萬世惜。
units.en: Commentary: Daozong knew his son's worth yet could not see through Yixin's deceit, and in the end destroyed the bond between father and son—a loss the ages lament.
units.literal: The commentary says: Daozong knew the crown prince's worth yet could not discern Yixin's fraud, and in the end severed father-son kin—a thing for ten thousand generations to lament.

units.zh: 乙辛知為一身之計，不知有君臣之義，豈復知有太子乎！
units.en: Yixin cared only for himself and knew nothing of the duty between ruler and minister—how could he spare a thought for the crown prince!
units.literal: Yixin knew only schemes for his own person and did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister—how could he still know there was a crown prince!

units.zh: 奸邪之臣亂人家國如此，可不戒哉！
units.en: When treacherous ministers can overturn a household and a realm like this, who would not take warning!
units.literal: Wicked and treacherous ministers throw households and states into disorder like this—can one fail to take warning!

units.zh: 可不戒哉！
units.en: Who would not take warning!
units.literal: Can one fail to take warning!

units.zh: 晉王，小字敖盧斡，天祚皇帝長子，母曰文妃蕭氏。
units.en: The Prince of Jin, childhood name Aolugan, was Emperor Tianzuo's eldest son; his mother was Literary Consort of the Xiao clan.
units.literal: Prince of Jin, childhood name Aolugan, eldest son of Emperor Tianzuo, mother called Literary Consort of the Xiao clan.

units.zh: 甫髫齔，馳馬善射。
units.en: While still a child he rode hard and shot well.
units.literal: While still in childhood he galloped horses and was skilled in archery.

units.zh: 出為大丞相耶律隆運後，封晉王。
units.en: Having been made heir to Grand Chancellor Yelu Longyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
units.literal: Having been given out as heir to Grand Chancellor Yelu Longyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

units.zh: 性樂道人善，而矜人不能。
units.en: By nature he delighted in praising others' goodness and was forbearing toward those who lacked ability.
units.literal: By nature he delighted in praising others' goodness and was forbearing toward those who lacked ability.

units.zh: 時宮中見讀書者輒斥，敖盧斡嘗入寢殿，見小底茶剌閱書，因取觀。
units.en: At the time anyone caught reading in the palace was scolded; Aolugan once entered the sleeping quarters, saw junior attendant Chacha reading, and took the book to look.
units.literal: At the time anyone seen reading in the palace was rebuked; Aolugan once entered the sleeping hall, saw the junior attendant Chacha reading a book, and took it to look.

units.zh: 會諸王至，陰袖而歸之，曰：「勿令他人見也。」
units.en: When other princes arrived he quietly slipped it back into his sleeve and returned it, saying, "Do not let anyone else see this."
units.literal: When the princes arrived he secretly tucked it in his sleeve and returned it, saying, "Do not let others see it."

units.zh: 一時號稱長者。
units.en: For a time he was acclaimed as a man of mature character.
units.literal: For a time he was acclaimed as a man of mature character.

units.zh: 及長，積有人望，內外歸心。
units.en: As he grew up he won wide esteem, and court and country alike looked to him.
units.literal: When he grew up he accumulated public esteem, and within and without all turned their hearts to him.

units.zh: 保大元年，南軍都統耶律余睹與其母文妃密謀立之，事覺，余睹降金，文妃伏誅，敖盧斡實不與謀，免。
units.en: In Baoda year 1 Southern Army commander-in-chief Yelu Yudu and Aolugan's mother Literary Consort secretly plotted to put him on the throne; when the plot was exposed Yudu defected to Jin, Literary Consort was executed, and Aolugan, who had not joined the plot, was spared.
units.literal: In the first year of Baoda, Southern Army commander-in-chief Yelu Yudu and Aolugan's mother Literary Consort secretly plotted to install him; when the affair was discovered Yudu surrendered to Jin, Literary Consort was executed, and Aolugan had in truth not joined the plot and was spared.

units.zh: 二年，耶律撒八等復謀立，不克。
units.en: In the second year Yelu Saba and others again plotted to enthrone him but failed.
units.literal: In the second year Yelu Saba and others again plotted to install him and did not succeed.

units.zh: 上知敖盧斡得人心，不忍加誅，令縊殺之。
units.en: Knowing Aolugan had won the people's hearts and unable to bear executing him openly, the emperor ordered him strangled.
units.literal: The sovereign knew Aolugan had won the people's hearts and could not bear to punish him directly, and ordered him strangled.

units.zh: 或勸之亡，敖盧斡曰：「安忍為蕞爾之軀，而失臣子之大節！」
units.en: Some urged him to flee; Aolugan said, "How could I save this petty life and betray the great duty of subject and son!"
units.literal: Some urged him to flee; Aolugan said, "How could I bear to save this petty body and lose the great integrity of subject and son!"

units.zh: 遂就死。
units.en: He then went to his death.
units.literal: He then accepted death.

units.zh: 聞者傷之。
units.en: All who heard of it grieved for him.
units.literal: Those who heard of it grieved for him.

units.zh: 論曰：天祚不君，臣下謀立其子，適以殺之。
units.en: Commentary: Tianzuo failed as a ruler; his ministers plotted to put his son on the throne—and thereby brought about the son's death.
units.literal: The commentary says: Tianzuo did not act as ruler; his ministers plotted to install his son, and thereby brought about his death.

units.zh: 敖盧斡重君父之命，不亡而死，申生其恭矣乎！
units.en: Aolugan honored his sovereign and father, refusing flight though it meant death—was he not as dutiful as Prince Sheng of Jin!
units.literal: Aolugan honored the command of ruler and father, not fleeing yet dying—was he not as dutiful as Shen Sheng!
